The First-Sale Cheat Sheet

Your whole path to sale #1, on one page. No ads, no list, no website.

You don't have a traffic problem. You don't have a talent problem. You have a first-sale problem. And it's smaller than you think.

Work through the seven steps in order. Each one has an example, and the first two have an AI prompt you can copy.

01 Pick a pain, not a passion

Your first product isn't your life's work. It fixes one annoying, specific problem for one specific person. AI prompt: "List 20 small problems [your audience] complains about online. Which 3 would someone pay $7 to fix this week?"

BeforeSocial media help.
After5 Instagram Story frames that get DMs for home bakers.

02 Make the smallest possible thing

One PDF, one template or one checklist, built in an afternoon with tools you already have. If it takes more than a day, you're overbuilding. AI prompt: "Write a one-page fix for [problem]. Plain words. Steps only. Include one example."

BeforeA 12-module course you'll finish "next month."
AfterA one-page Story Frame Kit with 5 fill-in-the-blank frames.

03 Price it like a snack, not a steak

$7 to $27. Low enough that yes is easy. High enough that it's real money from real buyers. When in doubt, start at $7.

04 Set up one checkout link

You need a way to take payment and deliver the file. That's it. Gumroad, Payhip or Whop each do both, and none of them need a website.

05 Go where the pain already lives

Don't build an audience first. Find a Facebook group, a comment section or a hashtag where your person is already complaining. Answer 5 real questions there, for free. Then say: "I had this same problem, so I made a 1-page kit that fixed it. Happy to send it if you want."

06 Start 10 conversations

Message 10 people who asked, commented or complained. Ask one easy question. No pitch.

BeforeHey! I made a product you'll love. Want to buy it?
AfterSaw your comment about [problem]. Is that still bugging you?

07 Sell before you're ready

Your first sale will feel too early. Good. "Ready" is where first sales go to die. Post the offer, send the messages, and fix the product after somebody buys it.

Before you close this page: one problem picked, small thing built, price set, checkout link working, 5 helpful answers posted, 10 conversations started. Stuck on a step? Reply to the email this came in and tell me the number. I read every reply.
